title: Read: person
description: One hero, dread, NPC or villain by uid, with liveness resolved through the one predicate. Answered by POST /world/person (Sim/icarus_sim/terrain_read.person_request). Four blocks answer 'is this person still here' in three vocabularies and status means two different things at two depths of one block; a caller must never have to know which applies to the record it just received.

block.description: The list this record came from, which is what terrain_liveness dispatches on. dreads is the antagonist cast inside the heroes block and shares its vocabulary.

person.description: The generator's own record, verbatim. Fields are the writing package's and are not restated here.

liveness.description: terrain_liveness.liveness(record, block). An absent status reads as present: a record written before its package recorded departure described someone who stood.

anchor.description: Where this person stands, spelled out as a terrain node wherever one is knowable, because everything else about a person's placement renumbers or is in another package's namespace.

source.description: The field the node was read from: villains.people[].node, npcs.people[].presence_node, npcs.sites[].node, or settlements.sites[].uid / ruins[].uid for a cast record resolved through its presence or its home. A ruined city keeps its uid and its node when it moves to ruins, so a presence naming a dead city still places.

uid.description: The place uid the anchor was resolved through, where one was used.

unresolved_uid.description: A presence naming somewhere no block here has a row for - a camp, college, port, shrine or nest. Reported rather than approximated by the home, because the home is a real place and the wrong one.
